TBF I don't even think this was done by accident CLI — 0.157.0, installed via npm install -g @openai/codex , Linux (WSL2) Please make daemon_auto_start opt-in (default false ) for the CLI , or at least ask once before turning it on. Since 0.157.0, just opening an interactive codex session: For a CLI, the least surprising default is that the backend lives and dies with the window, runs the binary I installed, and doesn't update itself in the background. A shared, self-updating daemon makes sense for Remote Control / the desktop app, so it would be fine to enable it there, or when the user explicitly runs codex app-server daemon start / bootstrap . If it stays on by default, please at least: Bug found while turning it off: codex app-server daemon stop stops the app-server but leaves the pid-update-loop updater running (still alive 70 s later, had to kill it manually). Workaround I'm using: codex features disable daemon_auto_start codex app-server daemon stop pkill -f ' app-server daemon pid-update-loop ' # not stopped by `daemon stop` rm -rf ~ /.codex/packages/app-server-daemon With the flag off, a new TUI session no longer spawns a daemon. I can confirm this on Windows 10 LTSC with Codex CLI 0.157.0 Setting daemon_auto_start = false in config.toml resolves the issue Two improvements would help: This would preserve the security restrictions without disrupting the normal CLI workflow. @tagorr Indeed — both 1 and 2 would work~ codex: disable daemon auto-start by default The Codex CLI is unusable due to this bug on Windows. This is terrible. I can't input anything on the CLI at all. You should fix this problem as soon as possible and give us 100 banked reset! There is a useful provenance boundary behind this request: installed CLI identity != daemon execution identity Once the CLI copies itself into a managed release directory and a background updater can replace that copy, the process that services a later turn is no longer necessarily the artifact the user explicitly installed or invoked. I would make the daemon expose a small execution receipt for each client attachment containing at least: client_cli_version + daemon_binary_digest + daemon_generation + updater_state + inherited_environment_generation Then a client can distinguish: A strong regression would start the daemon under environment A, attach from environment B, update the installed CLI, and verify that the client can see exactly which daemon generation/binary/environment is authoritative for the turn rather than inferring it from the foreground CLI version.
